ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BCA=90^\circ$, $BC=8$, and $AC=6$. Point $D$ is the midpoint on side $AB$, and point $E$ is a moving point on side $BC$. Connect $DE$, and fold $\triangle BDE$ along $DE$ to get $\triangle FDE$. As shown in figure (1), segment $DF$ intersects segment $BC$ at point $G$. When $BE=2$, what is the value of $\frac{GE}{GD}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BCA=90^\circ$, $BC=8$, and $AC=6$. Point $D$ is the midpoint of side $AB$, and point $E$ is a moving point on side $BC$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are three folding schematic diagrams; figure ① corresponds to the situation stated in the problem: in triangle ABC, D is on AB, E is on BC, after folding point F is obtained, and line segment DF intersects BC at G; what the problem asks for is GE/GD in figure ① when BE=2. Then reason: establish a coordinate system according to the method draft, take C=(0,0), B=(8,0), A=(0,6). Because D is the midpoint of AB, D=((0+8)/2,(6+0)/2)=(4,3). Because BE=2 and BC=8, and E is on BC, E=(6,0). The crease DE passes through D(4,3) and E(6,0), and its equation is 3x+2y-18=0. Folding reflects B to F, that is, F is the symmetric point of B=(8,0) with respect to the line DE. Using the point-to-line reflection formula, obtain F=(68/13,-24/13). Next find G: G is the intersection point of the line DF and BC, and BC is the x-axis, that is, y=0. Parametrize DF as D+t(F-D), that is, (4,3)+t(16/13,-63/13). Let y=0, then 3-63t/13=0, so t=13/21. Thus the x-coordinate of G is 4+(13/21)(16/13)=100/21, that is, G=(100/21,0). Therefore GE=6-100/21=26/21; GD=sqrt((100/21-4)^2+3^2)=sqrt((16/21)^2+9)=65/21. So GE/GD=(26/21)/(65/21)=2/5.
